correctness.rationale: Averaging rotation conjugates preserves feasibility and cannot increase the operator norm on the nonconstant subspace. The circulant Fourier drops are a(2−2 cos(πj/m))+2b[j odd]. The signed modes 1−Ea, 1−Ua−2b and −1+Va+2b have positive weighted average (V−U)/(V+2E−U) with relative weights (V−U)/E, 1, 1. Equality fixes both edge probabilities. The holding numerator is E for odd m, E−U for even m. The unused even-frequency maximum drop has coefficient F; V+E−U−F is E for odd m and 4c(1−c) for even m, where c=cos(π/m), so no omitted mode violates the bound, including m=4. For the prism the endpoints are E for nonconstant symmetric layer modes and 0 and Δ in the antisymmetric layer; the same weighted argument gives Δ/(Δ+2E). The unused symmetric minimum is no smaller than its antisymmetric counterpart, and prism holding is feasible since Δ+E≥4 (for odd m use Δ=4−U and E>U). Substitution verifies the holding/rung swap, exact even advantage and its π⁴ limit. Taylor expanding E∼4π²/m² and U∼π²/m² verifies the mass and gap limits and the fourfold gain against the optimal cycle. Only rotation-invariant uniqueness follows.
residual_risks: No claim about arbitrary optimizer uniqueness, nonreversible chains or finite-time total-variation optimum.

No separate optimization or sharpness step remains once the two exact optima are known.

They quantify a vanishing optimal rung mass and a fourth-order parity effect not captured by gap order alone. This assesses the content of the theorem, not the novelty of restating it from the two available optima.
